article.title: Romania: a growing hub of complicity in genocide
article.author: Vlad Muresan
article.content: In April 2026, the opening of yet another Israeli weapons factory in Romania was cause for celebration for some. With great fanfare, Elbit Systems – Israel’s largest private arms manufacturer – inaugurated its seventh production facility in the country, in the small town of Chitila, just outside Bucharest. The company whose weapons have helped sustain Israel’s genocide in Palestine, its decades-long occupation, and its military assaults on Iran was welcomed as a symbol of industrial progress. The event was marked by the test flight of a Watchkeeper X drone and was attended by high ranking Elbit officials, including Uri Maman, VP head of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Operations. The chair of the Senate Defense Committee, a former prime minister and defense minister, as well as an adviser to the serving defense minister were also in attendance. The event received extensive coverage across Romania’s major news outlets. Source: Nicoleta Pauliuc/Facebook At the time of the inauguration, the delivery of Romania’s unmanned aerial systems was already approximately ten months overdue. To date, Elbit has yet to deliver any of the contracted drones, with the delay now extending to 16 months. The company has cited force majeure arising from the war to justify this. In previous months, a significant number of similar Elbit drones were downed over Lebanon, Iran and Iraq. Elbit arms Israel’s attacks beyond Palestine. In Lebanon, its munitions were identified in attacks that killed a Reuters journalist and seven relief volunteers . In Syria, its drones conduct surveillance and strikes. In Iran, its armed drones, surveillance and electronic warfare systems supported Israel’s offensive. Through production, procurement and military cooperation, Romania helps sustain an industry that enables Israel’s regional offensives well beyond Gaza and Palestine. Once a socialist state committed to anti-imperialism, Romania has become an important link in the projection of US imperial power across West Asia, serving as both an operating base for US military aircraft and a production and supply hub within Israel’s military-industrial network. A network of complicity Owned by Simultec, one of the three Romanian Elbit Systems subsidiaries, the Chitila factory is the result of a €380 million contract signed by the Romanian state with the company for seven Watchkeeper X unmanned aerial systems. Romanian production of Watchkeeper X drones spans several companies in Elbit’s supply chain: Simultec manufactures composite airframes, A-E Electronics supplies aircraft components, Eurobody Hydraulics produces ground control stations, and Aerostar integrates the drones’ systems. Watchkeeper X presentation in Chitila, Romania. Source: Elbit System In 2024 and 2025, Israel was Romania’s main military export destination. Military equipment and technology worth over €150 million have been shipped from Romania to Israel. Most of these shipments are presumably coming from Elbit’s own Romanian subsidiaries, which are shipping back to Israel military electronics, drone components and mortar systems for integration into weapons platforms. In the first half of 2026, military exports from Romania to Israel amounted to €34 million. Romania authorized €307.24 million in military exports to Israel in 2025 – nearly 99% through global licenses allowing repeated shipments over several years – and a further €53.6 million in the first half of 2026. Romanian military exports to Israel 2025-2026. Source: ANCEX, Romania’s Department for Export Controls, within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. This newest expansion is symptomatic of a process that has been taking place all across Central and Eastern Europe. Under the guise of rearmament, Israeli companies are moving into the area securing record contracts and expanding their production facilities across the region, with Romania becoming one of its central pillars. Read more: Amid mass protests in the West, Israel’s military footprint expands in Eastern Europe This process further integrates the region into the imperialist world system that enabled the genocide in Gaza, while reinforcing Israel’s impunity and undermining international law and institutions. European rearmament creates new opportunities for complicity European rearmament is opening new markets for Israeli arms manufacturers, including through programmes presented as strengthening Europe’s industrial autonomy. Romania’s allocation of up to €16.68 billion in EU-backed loans under Security Action for Europe (SAFE) illustrates the scale of the opportunity. In May 2026, Romania’s General Aviation Inspectorate awarded a €43.18 million helicopter simulation contract to Simultec under the country’s SAFE investment plan. Although registered locally, the company belongs to the Israeli group. These connections also extend through European suppliers. A separate €30.7 million Romanian SAFE contract covers Vector drones from Germany’s Quantum Systems, whose published specifications identify Israel’s NextVision as the supplier of their electro-optical sensors. NextVision supplies imaging components to Elbit Systems, including for drones deployed in Gaza. In 2025, Norway’s largest pension fund, KLP, excluded the company over the risk that its products contribute to violations of international humanitarian law. Elbit Systems lightweight quadcopter. Source: Flightglobal.com Romania’s planned €3.337 billion SAFE procurement of Rheinmetall’s Lynx infantry fighting vehicles also has Israeli links. The configuration described in news reports incorporates Spike LR2 anti-tank missiles produced in cooperation with Israel’s Rafael Advance Defense Systems. In July 2025, Romania signed a €2.04 billion framework agreement for Rafael’s SPYDER air defense systems, followed by a first implementing contract worth approximately €600 million in June 2026. More Israeli companies moving in Israeli military and surveillance companies are expanding their presence in Romania beyond Elbit. IMCO has opened a component manufacturing facility in Crevedia, while Skylock is pursuing local counter-drone production and SAFE procurement opportunities with Optoelectronica. ParaZero and Aero Sentinel have demonstrated their technologies at Romanian military events and exercises. These are all companies deeply embedded in the Israeli military and responsible for genocide, apartheid and occupation in Palestine. Read more: In Eastern Europe, resistance grows to militarism and Israeli arms production The network also extends into surveillance: Cognyte operates a growing software development centre in Bucharest, while Romanian prosecutors have launched a procurement procedure for Cellebrite phone-extraction tools, whose use against journalists and activists abroad has raised serious human rights concerns. Some Romanians are resisting Elbit Out! is a campaign started in 2025 against a concrete infrastructure of complicity. It targets the fact that Israeli military companies are present in Romania, that they profit in Romania, that they produce in Romania, and that the Romanian government uses public money to strengthen them. Its internationalist approach connects solidarity with Palestine to opposition to the governments, corporations and military partnerships that sustain destruction across the Global South. It brings together struggles against war and austerity, demanding that public resources serve people’s needs. The Elbit Out! campaign published its second report in November 2026. Source: Elbit Out!/Facebook The campaign challenges the system that makes genocide profitable and turns Eastern Europe into a market, production base and source of debt for Western and Israeli weapons manufacturers. In November 2026, Elbit Out! published its second report , documenting how Romania has deepened its ties with Israel’s military-industrial complex through arms exports, public procurement and local weapons production. Released as the campaign enters its second year, the report exposes the growing gap between Romania’s professed commitment to international law and its continued economic and military cooperation with companies implicated in Israel’s crimes in Palestine and across the region.
